newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa to boost global logistics image.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa to boost global logistics image.

text.p: Lufthansa Cargo AG said it has launched a two-year marketing communications campaign to re-position the airline as a client-orientated global logistics supplier.

Michael Kraus, LCAG business development and global accounts manager told a news conference, that the "Thinking in New Directions" campaign aimed to change the airline's image from cargo transport operator to logistics services provider.

Marketing communications manager Michael Zengerle said the campaign, which will cost a seven-figure sum, highlights the airline's logistics know-how, destination network, the Flash time-definite express service, and ground handling speed and safety.
A survey by market research organisation Infratest Burke of 200 German shippers and forwarders showed Lufthansa Cargo came the closest to an ideal cargo airline, he said.
The German airline achieved the best mix of quality and safety but did not score so well on innovation and service orientation.
Kraus said it had been difficult for the cargo department of a passenger airline to operate in a market-orientated manner before becoming a separate company in January 1995.
The Lufthansa passenger division had decided routes, schedules and aircraft capacity and only German Cargo Airlines as a charter carrier operated in a client-orientated manner, he said.
But as an autonomous subsidiary of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, it was now necessary for Lufthansa Cargo to have modern marketing communications and to talk to its clients, he said.
Kraus built up the Lufthansa City Center travel agency chain and was passenger marketing manager before becoming the first Lufthansa Cargo business development manager in 1995.
Zengerle said that trade and consumer media advertising would focus on Europe, North America and Asia which generate 80 percent of the airline's revenue, he added.
Lufthansa Cargo would also direct-mail the pharmaceutical and semi-conductor industries and possibly the automobile industry by early 1997, he said.
The airline would take its first trade fair stand at a Japanese semi-conductor fair in the second half of 1997, he added. --Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax +44 171 542 5017
